subject: Q4 readiness: Acme QBR prep, renewal watchlist & exec asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Q4 readiness: Acme QBR - proposed agenda + asks

Hi Maya / Acme team,

Thanks again for partnering through the last quarter. We're scheduling a short QBR to align on health, usage trends, and the upcoming renewal. Proposed slot: Wed 12/22, 10:00-11:00 PT. Please confirm availability or propose alternatives.

Draft agenda (30-45 min):
- 5m: Introductions and objectives
- 10m: Usage & performance highlights (Redwood)
- 10m: Cost/optimization opportunities and proposed cadence
- 10m: Renewal timeline + procurement questions
- 5-10m: Exec/strategic asks and next steps

Immediate asks for the QBR prep:
- Can you confirm your expected renewal cadence (contract end date + procurement decision timeline)?
- Latest 30/60/90 day usage numbers (token consumption or calls/month) — if you can share a simple export, that helps our cost/forecast model.
- Any new procurement or security requirements we should include in the deck?

Attached: QBR_customer_health_snapshot_Acme_2026.pdf — internal health & latency summary.

We'll have Jordan join to discuss renewal options and Karthik to align on OKR-driven product asks.

Thanks — look forward to your availability.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: QBR_customer_health_snapshot_Acme_2026.pdf (PDF)

From: Maya Patel <maya@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q4 readiness: Acme QBR - proposed agenda + asks

Hi Marissa — thanks for the note and draft agenda. 12/22 10:00 PT works for the core team; I'll loop in procurement for scheduling confirmation.

Answers:
- Renewal cadence: Contract current term ends 2027-02-28; procurement is targeting a decision by 2027-01-31 to hit budgeting cycles.
- Usage: I'll export a high-level call/token report for 11/1–12/9 and share by 12/14 (we have a spike tied to a promotional test in early Nov).
- Security: Nothing new beyond the SOC2 artifact requests — procurement may ask for a short log-retention statement.

Procurement attached our internal timeline (Acme_Renewal_Timeline_Dec2026.pdf). Please send an updated quote reflecting committed monthly throughput options (we're evaluating a dedicated pool).

Maya
Maya Patel
Head of AI Product, Acme Corp
maya@acmecorp.com

Attachments: Acme_Renewal_Timeline_Dec2026.pdf (PDF)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Acme QBR prep — renewal risk & proposed mitigations

Marissa / Karthik — quick assessment after reviewing the snapshot and the timeline. High level: medium risk. Key signals:
- Usage volatility: 40% month-over-month variance tied to Nov test; base consumption down ~12% vs. forecast.
- Cost sensitivity flagged by procurement — asked for committed options and discounts.
- One reported latency incident in October (resolved), but exec-level concern remains.

Proposed mitigation actions:
1) Offer a short-term credit for the Nov overage and present a 6/12-month committed tier with transparent burst pricing.
2) Prepare a one-pager on our reliability fixes and SLA targets — include incident timeline and remediation steps.
3) Recommend an executive presence at the QBR (VP Customer Success) for the renewal discussion if Acme indicates procurement pressure.

I've attached a light risk register with current status and owner for each ask: renewal_risk_register_Acme_2026.csv.

If we agree, I'll draft the exec ask language and the committed-tier quote for Marissa to send to procurement.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Success Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: renewal_risk_register_Acme_2026.csv (CSV)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Internal: Acme QBR prep — renewal risk & proposed mitigations

Thanks Jordan — this is helpful. Quick internal plan so we have a clean exec-ready package by 12/21 (one business day before QBR):
- Karthik: Can you produce a 2-slide OKR alignment that shows how Acme maps to our platform adoption OKRs + recommended product asks (due 12/20 EOD)? Keep it short: metric → impact → proposal.
- Grace: Please pull customer health metrics (30/60/90 day usage, latency % over SLO, support tickets trend) and update the snapshot. Put the export in the Drive folder linked below.
- Jordan: Draft the exec ask email and the committed-tier quote (include a 6-month and 12-month option with pricing delta and transparent burst terms). I'll own procurement outreach.

I'll assemble an "exec asks" summary doc and the final QBR deck. I've started an exec-asks-summary_20261218.md in the shared Drive. Plan to include:
- One-line renewal risk classification + recommended concession
- Supporting metrics (usage, incidents, cost)
- Next steps with owners and dates

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAcmeQBRPrep

Marissa

Forwarding the internal risk register and the snapshot in case procurement wants to preview.
